title: Machine learning target deconvolution identifies GAK as a kinase dependency in DLBCL
summary: A phenotypic screen of kinase probes across diffuse large B-cell lymphoma models, analyzed with the iterative machine-learning method idTRAX, identified cyclin G-associated kinase (GAK) as a tumor-selective target. GAK inhibition caused G2/M arrest and cell death, stronger in RB-null cells, and GAK inhibitors including repurposed clinical compounds showed single-agent anti-DLBCL activity in vivo. Only the abstract was reviewed and idTRAX details were not read.
ai_technology: idTRAX iterative machine-learning target deconvolution of kinase-probe phenotypic screens
organization: Sheila and David Fuente Graduate Program in Cancer Biology, Miami, FL, USA

evidence.tested: Mechanistic cell studies and in vivo single-agent activity of GAK inhibitors in DLBCL models.
evidence.unknown: Clinical efficacy in patients; model details of idTRAX. Full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deconvoluted screening data to rank kinases for tumor selectivity and nominate GAK.
